name: MIGRATION_REMEDIATION_OPTIONS

options.name: Clean baseline reset
options.concept: Archive current migration history outside the active Prisma migration path. Generate a new baseline (single migration) that represents the approved current schema. Fresh DBs apply the new baseline. Existing DBs undergo read-only schema-parity validation and then a controlled, operator-authorized `migrate resolve --applied` for the new baseline row.
options.persistent_db_action: One-time, operator-authorized `prisma migrate resolve --applied <baseline>` after schema-parity validation. NOT executed in Phase 8B.
options.migration_metadata_action: Reset `_prisma_migrations` rows for existing DBs by re-resolving against the new baseline.
options.fresh_db_result: PASS — single baseline migration produces current schema in one step.
options.existing_db_result: PASS — schema already matches new baseline (verified via read-only parity check); one-time resolve marks the new baseline as applied.
options.data_loss_risk: None on schema; metadata is regenerated, not deleted.
options.checksum_risk: Low — old migration checksums are removed from active path; new baseline has one canonical checksum.
options.operational_complexity: Medium — requires operator procedure document + one-time resolve.
options.rollback: Re-archive new baseline; restore old chain from external archive.

options.name: Restore historical init_schema
options.concept: Reconstruct the original init_schema (without the retroactively-added columns). Remove from init every object owned by a later migration. Keep later additive migrations unchanged.
options.fresh_db_result: Depends on what 'original' init_schema contained. **There is no recoverable original** because git history contains exactly one version of init_schema.
options.existing_db_result: FAIL — existing DBs already have the expanded init_schema columns. Removing them from the migration file does not retroactively remove them from the DB. Prisma will report drift.
options.data_loss_risk: HIGH on schema (existing DBs already include the columns; if any procedure later tries to drop them, data is lost).
options.checksum_risk: HIGH — forges an 'original' init_schema checksum that was never committed.
options.rollback: Cannot roll back — once the init_schema file is rewritten, the historical content is lost (unless archived externally).

options.name: Make historical migrations conditional (IF NOT EXISTS guards)
options.concept: Wrap each UNGUARDED_DUPLICATE operation with `IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF EXISTS` so the migration is idempotent against a schema that already has the columns/indexes.
options.fresh_db_result: PASS — guarded operations are no-ops against init_schema's expanded columns.
options.existing_db_result: PASS — guarded operations are no-ops against any existing schema.
options.checksum_risk: Medium — Prisma flags checksum changes for already-applied migrations. Environments with this migration in `_prisma_migrations` would need a `migrate resolve` (forbidden against persistent DB).
options.rollback: Revert the guards; replay against fresh DB.
options.recommendation: ACCEPTABLE SECONDARY — but does not address the deeper issue that the migration history is logically inconsistent (six migrations now do nothing useful because their work was already done by init_schema).

options.name: Entrypoint auto-resolve or skip
options.concept: Modify docker/api-entrypoint.sh to detect existing schema objects and automatically run `prisma migrate resolve` to skip the failed migration.
options.persistent_db_action: **YES — auto-modifies persistent DB** based on detection heuristics.
options.migration_metadata_action: Auto-resolves failed migrations based on schema state.
options.fresh_db_result: Does not apply — fresh DBs have no failed migrations to skip.
options.existing_db_result: **UNSAFE** — auto-resolve can mark a migration as applied when it has not been, hiding real schema drift; behavior varies per environment; audit trail is corrupted; legal-system deployment cannot rely on heuristic DB repair.
options.data_loss_risk: MEDIUM — wrong resolve marks a migration as applied when objects are not actually present; subsequent deploys may then drop or alter objects based on the lie.
options.checksum_risk: HIGH — silent checksum deviations from auto-resolve.
options.operational_complexity: Low (one shell script) but introduces a hidden, environment-specific repair mechanism.
options.rollback: Possible but audit trail is permanently lost once resolve runs.
options.recommendation: REJECTED — hides migration history defects; unsafe for legal-system production deployment.

options.name: Fresh-install bootstrap outside Prisma
options.concept: Import a schema dump (mysqldump or `prisma db pull` artifact) directly into a fresh DB. Then run `prisma migrate resolve --applied` for every historical migration to mark them as applied. Continue with future Prisma migrations.
options.persistent_db_action: One-time schema import (if dump replaces existing DB) OR one-time `migrate resolve` (if existing DB already has the schema).
options.migration_metadata_action: Mark all current migrations as applied in `_prisma_migrations`.
options.fresh_db_result: PASS — schema import + resolve marks the chain as applied; future migrations work normally.
options.existing_db_result: PASS — schema already matches; resolve marks the chain as applied.
options.data_loss_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — if a fresh-DB bootstrap ever points at an existing DB, the dump import will overwrite it. Operator procedure MUST guard against this.
options.checksum_risk: Low (the new chain reuses current checksums).
options.operational_complexity: Medium-High — requires a canonical schema dump artifact, versioned alongside code.
options.recommendation: ACCEPTABLE ALTERNATIVE — effectively the same outcome as Option A but heavier operational footprint. Choose this only if Option A is forbidden by user policy.

recommendation_rationale: Option A is the only option that produces a logically consistent migration history with one canonical baseline.
Option A is the only option that supports all four environment states (A/B/C/D) without fabricating history or relying on hidden heuristics.
Option A minimizes per-deployment risk: fresh DBs succeed in a single migration; existing DBs require exactly one operator-authorized action.
Option A preserves the principle that migrations should be immutable once committed; the new baseline is a new migration, not an edit of an old one.
Option A's data-loss risk is bounded (zero on schema; zero on data because the operator resolve marks the baseline as applied without modifying schema).
Options B and D are rejected because they fabricate history (B) or hide defects behind heuristics (D).
Options C and E are acceptable fallbacks if Option A is forbidden by user policy, but neither addresses the underlying logical inconsistency.
